name: eclipticam-v1
pedestal_notes: CHART FLOOR ONLY, on the v1 CONTAINER basis: 10-frame coadds, uint32, still MSB-aligned (deliberately NOT repacked 2026-08-20 — shifting moves the whole basis and is a calibration decision). 10180 / 10 coadds / 64 (MSB) = 15.9 per frame. Not comparable to any v3w pedestal.
black_level_notes: OV5647 electronic zero, PER FRAME in 10-bit LSB-aligned ADU. Two independent measurements agree: 10180/10/64 = 15.9 here, and starcam ov5647_4x_coadd floor 61.184/4 = 15.30. ~16, the usual OV5647 black level — NOT 64 (see eclipticam/camera.json for how that error arose).
blackest_observed_notes: Unknown — no eclipticam v1 frames in the quality DB. Scan the v1 tree to fill this in.
plate_scale_notes: OV5647 stock lens, 53.50 deg horizontal / 2592 px (official RPi figure).
max_single_exposure_notes: picamera2 video-config ceiling ~3.07 s; longer integrations must use the streaming coadd path.
rotate_180_notes: Camera sensor is physically mounted upside down. In-capture 180° rotation is applied (rpicam-still --rotation 180). No downstream rotation in processing.
night_layout_notes: TRANSITIONAL: live eclipticam/capture.py still writes to night/<night>/v1/HH/NNNN.fits.fz and day/<date>/v1/HH/NNNN.jpg. The post-split camera name 'eclipticam-v1' resolves the legacy 'v1' subcam via the percam reader. Once capture is migrated, flip to 'canonical' (per DECISIONS.md 2026-06-16).
state_notes: Shares the sky with eclipticam-v3w; night starts at sun -10 deg (was the -12 default). v1 is day-only so this mainly keeps the two cameras' state machines consistent.
